1.note: In b. Ketubbot 19b the saying is attributed to R. Ammi; the author's attribution to R. Yose is kept.

2.note: Readings of this name vary in Seder Olam manuscripts (often understood as Severus or as a corruption of another name); transliterated.

3.note: Apparently the Montalboddo family; the identification of these owners is uncertain.

4.note: Possibly Abraham Farissol's polemical work Magen Avraham, but the identification is not certain.

5.note: Sense obscure; possibly referring to Maimonides' principle that an isolated aggadic statement may be figurative.

6.note: Evidently the Alexander Romance (Pseudo-Callisthenes) in some version; the phrase 'by the Egyptian magicians' is the author's description.

7.he: ב' הדפוסים הראשונים של אברהם כונ"ת
7.note: Abraham Conat printed the editio princeps of Josippon at Mantua (c. 1476-80); the reference to 'two first printings' is unclear.
